hypothese.summary: Raw-material inflation shock (Middle East, base oil) managed through accelerated price increases vs 2021-22; 2026 revenue inflated by pricing (guidance >3,7 Md€, probably close to 4 Md€) but EBIT nearly flat (~450 M€), hence a transitory margin compression; 100% integration of OPET-FUCHS Turkey under way.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
FUCHS is a pricing-power bet under an exogenous shock, now validated: since the Middle East conflict inflated base-oil and petrochemical costs (Feb 2026), the group has repriced faster than in 2021-22 and delivered the best first half in its history (H1 26: sales EUR 2,003M +11%, EBIT EUR 260M +24%, margin 13.0% vs 11.6%) - enough for management to RAISE FY26 EBIT guidance to EUR 460-480M (from ~450M) while keeping the revenue call 'significantly above EUR 3.7bn'. The second leg is capitalistic: OPET-FUCHS (Turkey) moved from 50% equity-method to full consolidation (closed 30/04/2026), adding ~EUR 100M annualized revenue. Management's own honesty frames the risk: only ~1/3 of the Q2 organic surge is genuine demand - the rest is pre-buying and customers switching from supply-constrained competitors, with uncertain retention - and a period of relative margin decline is expected as the pass-through lag catches up. The family-controlled structure (voting ordinaries held by the Fuchs family; listed prefs) is a permanent fact without projection impact.

== THESIS READ ==
- FY26 EBIT guidance raised to EUR 460-480M on a record H1 - the pricing-power thesis is delivering ahead of plan.
- Management deflates its own beat: ~2/3 of the Q2 surge flagged as temporary (pre-buying, competitor shortages), H2 normalization expected - a rare conservatism marker, to test at FY close.
- Saudi JV fire (32% stake): no production for the rest of 2026, rebuild into 2027 - ~1.5% of group EBIT, absorbed within guidance.
- Horizon extended to 2030 at this refresh (was 2027-only): +3-3.5% sales, margin grinding to 12.8%, on the FUCHS100 trajectory.
- Watch: retention of competitor-switch volumes and the pass-through lag on H2 margins - the two swing factors management itself refuses to quantify.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: published IFRS, aligned with data (no management 'underlying' adjustments). Bridge (c-ter): 2025 reconciles cleanly (tax 29%, small net financial charge); projections at 28.5% normative tax, net financial result ~0. FY26 = guidance midpoint (EBIT 470, sales ~4,05bn); 2027 kept from the prior thesis (normalization year); 2028-2030 added at this refresh (AN-EXTENSION-2028-2030). omniumND 2026 stays WEAKLY SOURCED (OPET cash-out undisclosed - AN-OPET-ND, priority fix). Scorecard: EBIT-anchored (no EPS guidance), FY26 anchor EUR 450M posed; closed-FY history not sourced at setup - first measurable observation at FY26 close; application suspended (documented). Semiannual EPS split deferred: H1 net income not captured from the sources used this refresh (transcript + press) - build it at the next refresh from the H1 report (E5 ter), together with the GAAP/IFRS statements pass (etatsFinanciers queue). WATCH-LIST: (1) H2 repricing magnitude vs the guided normalization; (2) OPET final price and true net debt; (3) whether sales cross EUR 4bn (lower bound of the FUCHS100 2031 target, 5 years early); (4) working-capital drift (target 20% of sales); (5) buyback resumption. Next useful refresh: Q3 2026 (late October).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 2026 (late Oct): first read on H2 normalization vs the raised guidance; OPET first full quarter; FY26 dividend trajectory (25th consecutive increase targeted).

dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 EBIT raised to EUR 460-480M; sales significantly above EUR 3.7bn. Management cautions H1 strength is partly temporary (pre-buying, competitors' raw-material shortages).
pointsCles: Record H1: sales EUR 2,003M (+11%, organic +12% volume-driven across all three regions), EBIT EUR 260M (+24%, 13.0% margin vs 11.6%) - best first half in group history, with functional costs up only 5% against 11% sales growth; reported H1 EPS EUR 1.36.

Management's key decomposition of the Q2 surge (+21% y/y): only ~1/3 genuine business growth, ~1/3 PRE-BUYING (to reverse in H2 - 'more volume in H1, less in H2, equalized over the year'), ~1/3 customers switching from supply-constrained competitors (partial retention expected but unquantified) - with the explicit double warning: do NOT extrapolate H1, and do NOT take the implied H2 (EUR 200-220M) as the 2027-28 earnings base; read 2026 as a whole (guidance raised to EUR 460-480M EBIT).

Middle East supply crisis is the swing factor: Group III base oils and PAO short, no normalization expected before MID-2027 even if the conflict ends; several price-increase rounds already implemented (~25-30% of sales on monthly price-variation clauses), Q2 net price-vs-cost effect POSITIVE, but the CEO flags a coming 2021-22-style relative-margin valley - Q3 is the critical quarter to watch; logistics costs are not passed through.

Fire at the Saudi JV plant (Yanbu, 32% stake, announced the morning of the call): no output for the rest of 2026, rebuild taking a year plus, ~1.5% of group EBIT - guidance CONFIRMED; balance-sheet note: net liquidity down to EUR 13M (from 151M) after EUR 160M dividends, the OPET Turkey buyout and inflation-driven working capital (+EUR 139M NOWC build; H1 FCF before acquisitions EUR 61M vs 81M).
